Machines that run agents · required
  Agents run on machines; the hub's own machine can be one.
<QR>
  1. Add a machine
     The hub's own machine can run agents too. In the app, Settings › Hub › Machines › Add machine does each of these.
     The hub's own machine, on it:
       fleetd machine add --local
     Another machine, on the hub:
       fleetd pair --worker <name>
       The hub is only at http://HUB, which no other machine reaches, so only a node on the hub's own computer can join it. For another machine, give the hub its tailnet or LAN address: on the hub, run fleetd init --listen <ip>:<port> --url http://<name>:<port> (Settings › Hub › Setup › Where the hub listens), then try again.
<QR>
  2. Android screens (optional)
     Android emulators need Linux with KVM. Turn them on on the machine's page in Settings › Hub › Machines. iOS simulators are the agents' Mac's: A Mac for agents sets it up.
<QR>
  In the app: Settings › Hub › Machines.
✗  Machines that run agents required: Agents run on machines; the hub's own machine can be one. Fix: fleetd init --step machines

Run fleetd init --step machines again when you've done it; it keeps what's done.
